answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making each identity expensive: to register, an agent must lock a stake and solve a fresh cipher puzzle tied to its public key, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes and a thousand puzzles. Like a lotus that only opens when the water is deep enough, participation only blooms after real cost is paid. A falcon-fast verifier then checks the stake and puzzle on-chain before the identity can earn, so cheap clones are filtered out before they can vote or mine.
